accepted_precision.method: stratified estimate weighted by distinct resolutions per tier; interval propagated from per-tier Wilson bounds, not a normal approximation
accepted_precision.caveat: the sample is drawn by a disproportionate per-tier quota, so this reweighting is required; it is also what makes the figure higher than the raw rows, so read it next to raw_sample_precision below. The interval is a weighted sum of per-tier Wilson bounds: conservative, but not a calibrated 95% interval
accepted_precision.bootstrap_note: stratified bootstrap over the sampled rows, 20,000 resamples. Narrower, and blind to errors in tiers that scored 100% in the sample

as_labelled_raw_precision.note: every labelled accepted row, scored on the resolution it had when labelled. On the held-out test sample this is the frozen measurement of the pipeline before the audit repairs; it does not describe the current pipeline

stale_labels.note: rows whose resolution has changed since they were labelled; excluded from every figure above and listed for re-labelling

raw_sample_precision.note: the unweighted result over the rows a human actually read. 36 of the 54 current rows in this sample sit in an accepting tier; the rest are refusals and are scored separately. The sample size is 58 (4 stale), the precision denominator is 36 -- these are different numbers and quoting the first as the second overstates the evidence

withheld_tier_quality.reading: most proposals held for review are wrong, which is the evidence that the automatic threshold is not set too low

limitations: labels assigned by one reviewer (the pipeline author); no second annotator

FUZZY_AUTO, SALT_STRIPPED and CLEANED have so few distinct values that the development sample consumed all of them; their rates are carried over and are therefore optimistic, since the rules were tuned on exactly those rows
reference vocabulary is scoped to NSCLC drug candidates, so a correct refusal to resolve an out-of-scope drug counts as missing coverage, not as an error
sampling is stratified by tier, so tier-level rates are far more precise than the rare tiers' raw counts suggest, but tiers with very few distinct values still carry wide intervals
